details:
A scrollable log of chatbox messages sent in the current instance, accessible from the menu.

Problem

Chatbox messages appear as a bubble above the sender's head and disappear after a fixed interval. This has real visibility problems:

Bubbles are occluded by world geometry and by other avatars

They become unreadable at distance, which is worst in crowded instances

Simultaneous messages overlap each other

If you were looking elsewhere, or had your menu open, the message is simply gone

Long messages, or messages in a language you don't read fluently, expire before you finish

From the sender's side, there's no way to know whether a message was seen. When nobody responds, you can't tell whether you were ignored or whether the bubble was never visible, so you retype it.

Accessibility

The chatbox is a primary communication channel for users who can't rely on voice:

Deaf and hard-of-hearing users, for whom it's one of the few ways to follow what others say

Users who can't speak, or can't speak in their current environment

Non-native speakers who need time to read or translate

For all of these, "gone once it disappears" is a direct disadvantage. Voice conversation allows asking someone to repeat themselves; the chatbox has no equivalent.

Implementation note

The messages already travel over the network. Today they're rendered and then discarded. Retaining them client-side and listing them requires no new transmission and no server-side change.

What's needed:

Sender name, message body, timestamp

A scrollable list, with a capped retention count

Cleared on leaving the instance; persistence beyond that can be a separate opt-in

Consistency with mute and block

Messages from blocked users should not appear in the log. The same should likely apply to muted users. Existing safety settings need to carry over so the log doesn't become a new vector for harassment.

Related: bubble duration

Separately from the log, letting users adjust how long bubbles stay visible would help. The current duration is fixed and doesn't account for varying reading speed. A log would reduce the urgency of this, but it stands on its own.
title: Chat history log for chatbox messages
